1.why: Four different transition families with no source, so I fell back on the commonest key style for this stem, exemplification ('For instance,').

2.why: 'In some circumstances, however,' is by far the longest and most specifically hedged option, and length/specificity is the usual key tell in a transition set.

3.why: 'On the contrary,' and 'Similarly,' are polar mates and 'In other words,' is restatement; 'For instance,' is the unpaired exemplifier.

4.why: Only C names an actual measurement procedure (satellite images 2000-2020, horizontal distance of the terminus); the others give purpose, cause, or a result.

5.why: Only B contains both halves of the contrast in one 'once...but...' construction; the others state just the new explanation.

6.why: Only C is a generalization across many cases (40 cities, a per-10-point cooling rate); A, B, D are single- or two-city anecdotes.

7.why: 'Thus' and 'Correspondingly' overlap as consequence/parallel, so the unpaired concessive 'Even so,' is the likely key.

8.why: 'After all' and 'As a result' both point back to cause and 'By comparison' needs a second case; the concessive 'Even so,' is the odd one out.

9.why: Genuine chance - four identically framed options differing only in numbers and weather condition; picked the most modest, internally plausible pairing (15 days, two years).

10.why: 'For this reason' and 'Thus' are duplicate causal options and cannot both be right, which leaves the contrast 'By contrast' over the restatement.

11.why: 'With few exceptions,' is the one non-standard, qualifying transition in an otherwise stock set (result/parallel/example).

12.why: Genuine chance - four parallel limitations differing only in cultivar and held-fixed variable; 'Salinas' with temperature held fixed is the most plausible lettuce shade study.

13.why: 'Similarly' and 'Thus' are the usual continuation distractors and 'In other words' restates; the contrastive 'Nevertheless,' stands alone.

14.why: Only C ties the specific example to the named principle ('though separated by over 400 million years, both independently evolved'); B states the principle with no example, A and D the example with no principle.

15.why: Only A puts both figures side by side ('up to 3,000 miles' vs 'as far as 9,000 miles'); B and C give one species each, D gives no distances.

16.why: Only A spans the pollution and the recovery (closed 1980, swimmers returned 2018); the others give a single point in the sequence.

17.why: 'Consequently' and 'Also' are addition/result mates and 'In other words' restates; the contrastive 'However,' is unpaired.

18.why: Only C states the whole chain (otters eat urchins, urchins graze kelp, kelp collapsed then rebounded); A, B, D each carry one link.

19.why: Only A actually rebuts the assumption ('Far from vanishing... rebounded to about 540,000 speakers'); the other three report declines.

20.why: Genuine chance - four options identical except for the organism and thickness; blue mussels dominating fouling growth by weight is the most plausible real finding.

21.why: All four are parallel caveats, but only B names the design flaw that actually blocks the causal claim ('no unlit path used for comparison'), which matches 'cannot yet be credited to the lighting.'

22.why: Only A links wolves to elk behavior to willow and aspen regrowth; B, C, D are isolated facts with no chain.

23.why: Only A names one cause driving multiple effects ('Rising ocean temperatures drove several changes at once'); the others merely note coincidence in 2016.

24.why: 'Consequently' and 'Likewise' are stock continuation distractors and 'In other words' restates, leaving the concessive 'That said,'.
